title: Airflow and surface are different
hook: Same towel, same cool air. Does a breeze make it dry sooner?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that moving air carries damp air away from the cloth so more water can leave each part of it, without changing how much cloth is exposed

misconception: A breeze only helps drying if the air is warm.
objective: The model keeps cloth area fixed and changes the assumed mass-transfer flux. Area and transfer conditions multiply; changing one does not secretly change the other.

claims.text: The model keeps the cloth area fixed and changes only how fast the moving air takes water away. Area and air movement multiply; changing one does not secretly change the other.
claims.source: OpenStax College Physics 2e §13.6, https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/13-6-humidity-evaporation-and-boiling (opened 2026-10-14). Evaporation is inhibited by humidity. The card's constant flux is an explicitly illustrative assumption, not a measured household drying rate. recall.question: A towel exposes 1.5 m² in still air. A fan doubles the model flux. What happens in the model?
options: Area becomes 3 m² and the rate doubles
Area stays 1.5 m² and the rate doubles
Area stays 1.5 m² and the rate is unchanged
recall.why: Rate = exposed area × flux. The fan changes flux, not area, so the rate doubles while the area stays 1.5 m². A face folded shut stays hidden however the air moves. The doubling is illustrative, not a fan measurement.
